name: Flow
description: One agent with the whole thread: plan, implement via subagent harnesses, verify its own diff, attach visual evidence, and hand to the PR gate. The simple arm of the staged-vs-simple comparison (TRIAL-RUNS).

work.title: Do the work
work.instructions:
You are the whole workflow in one session — you keep the thread, so never re-derive what you or a subagent already established.

1. Read the brief. Its "# Project" section carries the test command, branch rules, and preview-setup state — those are facts; trust them. Think the plan through; you do not need approval to start (the PR gate at the end is the checkpoint).
2. Implement: delegate non-trivial code changes to a subagent harness (pi or claude) with a precise task — you hold the context, it holds the editor. Small mechanical edits, run them yourself with bash.
3. Verify your own work: the diff against your plan, the project's test command, and — for visual changes — serve the preview (start_preview; the saved setup makes it one call) and capture before/after screenshots with agent-browser (follow its installed skill), attaching each with attach_screenshot. The gate reads those. A blocked visual check is a finding to report, not to engineer around: retry at most twice, attach what you saw, say so.
4. Declare the PR with propose_pr, then transition to the gate. Nothing is pushed until it approves.

pr-approve.title: Approve PR
pr-approve.instructions: The work's summary, the attached screenshots, and the PR proposal are shown. Approve it to push the branch and open the PR, send it back with a comment for changes, or reject to end the run.

next.when: Request changes (add a comment for the agent)

publish.title: Publish
publish.instructions: Deterministic: pushes the approved branch and opens the approved PR.
